verdicts.note: Attacked on magnitude: he has been the elected assessor for under a year (won the November 2025 vacancy election [S5]), so elected tenure is short. But the axis records proven record, and the dossier documents appraisal work in this office 2016-2023 plus 13 years in Chicago [S3], DOR accreditation since 2018 confirmed by an official record [S4], and incumbency [S5]. S3, S4 and S5 exist in his frontmatter and support the basis; three sources, two of them official, carry high. -2 high stands.

Direction holds: he challenges a sitting assessor [S5][S6] with DOR accreditation only since October 2024 [S2] and promises 'fresh ideas, better tools' [S4]. Evidence cuts against going higher: his own 2025 letter says the job 'requires real experience' and 'isn't a learning opportunity', and he described himself as working inside the Assessor's Office [S3], so he does not run as an outsider; +1, not +2. Wording flaw in the basis that does not change the score: 'against the incumbent' is anachronistic, since S4 is from June 2025, an open-seat race before Jenkins won; and the 'appraisal credentials of his own' clause rests on S3, which is not cited. S2 and S4 exist and support the rest. Medium fits, given every statement is from 2025 and none from 2026.
